# Identifying Important Predictors of Bioavailability

To determine the relative importance of each BLM predictor on trace element bioavailability, we will conduct a multiple linear regressions (MLR), determine their standardized beta coefficients, VIF, and relative importance

## 1. Build and the MLR

Use log-transformed and standardized variables

```{r}
library(MASS)
library(car)
library(relaimpo)
library(dplyr)
library(corrplot)

vars_to_select <- c("log_Cu_nM", "log_Temp_C", "pH", "log_DOC_nM",
                    "log_DIC_nM", "log_Cl_nM", "log_Ca_nM",
                    "log_Mg_nM", "log_SO4_nM", "log_Na_nM",
                    "log_K_nM")

# Standardize variables
std_vars <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(log_TBL_Cu_nmol_g, all_of(vars_to_select)) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric)) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ as.numeric(scale(.x)), .names = "{.col}_std")) %>%
  dplyr::select(ends_with("_std")) %>%
  as.data.frame()

# Define the standardized predictor names + standardized response
vars_to_select_std <- paste0(vars_to_select, "_std")
response_std <- "log_TBL_Cu_nmol_g_std"

# Model formula using standardized columns
form_std <- reformulate(vars_to_select_std, response = response_std)

# 1. Full MLR
full_mod <- lm(form_std, data = std_vars)
full_mod_summary <- summary(full_mod)

# 2. Estimates (standardized partial slopes) + p-values
coef_table <- full_mod_summary$coefficients

est_df <- data.frame(
  Predictor = rownames(coef_table),
  Estimate  = coef_table[, "Estimate"],
  p_value   = coef_table[, "Pr(>|t|)"]
) %>%
  filter(Predictor != "(Intercept)")

# 3. VIF
vif_vals <- vif(full_mod)

vif_df <- data.frame(
  Predictor = names(vif_vals),
  VIF       = as.numeric(vif_vals)
)

# 4. Relative importance (lmg)
rel_imp <- calc.relimp(full_mod, type = "lmg", rela = TRUE)

rel_df <- data.frame(
  Predictor = names(rel_imp$lmg),
  Rel_Importance = as.numeric(rel_imp$lmg)
)

# 5. Combine summary table
final_table <- est_df %>%
  left_join(vif_df, by = "Predictor") %>%
  left_join(rel_df, by = "Predictor") %>%
  arrange(desc(Rel_Importance))

final_table

# 6. Create full coefficient table for separate Excel sheet
coef_tab <- as.data.frame(full_mod_summary$coefficients)
coef_tab$Predictor <- rownames(coef_tab)
coef_tab <- coef_tab %>%
  relocate(Predictor)

# 7. Create model summary table for separate Excel sheet
model_stats <- data.frame(
  Metric = c(
    "Residual standard error",
    "R-squared",
    "Adjusted R-squared",
    "F-statistic",
    "Numerator df",
    "Denominator df"
  ),
  Value = c(
    full_mod_summary$sigma,
    full_mod_summary$r.squared,
    full_mod_summary$adj.r.squared,
    unname(full_mod_summary$fstatistic["value"]),
    unname(full_mod_summary$fstatistic["numdf"]),
    unname(full_mod_summary$fstatistic["dendf"])
  )
)

# 8. Save workbook
library(openxlsx)
out_dir <- "Multiple linear regression"
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

write.xlsx(
  list(
    Final_Table = final_table,
    Full_Model_Coefficients = coef_tab,
    Full_Model_Summary = model_stats
  ),
  file = file.path(out_dir, "MLR.xlsx"),
  overwrite = TRUE
)
```

## 3. Partial slope plots

Partial regression plots of log BLM parameters

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(broom)

# 1. Extract predictors
retained_vars <- names(coef(full_mod))[-1]  # drop intercept

# 2. Function to get partial residuals for each predictor
get_partial_df <- function(model, data, var) {
  # Construct model formula terms
  all_terms <- attr(terms(model), "term.labels")
  other_terms <- setdiff(all_terms, var)
  
  # Get residuals of Y on all predictors except the variable of interest
  y_formula <- reformulate(other_terms, response = all.vars(formula(model))[1])
  y_resid <- resid(lm(y_formula, data = data))
  
  # Get residuals of X_var on all other predictors
  x_formula <- reformulate(other_terms, response = var)
  x_resid <- resid(lm(x_formula, data = data))
  
  df <- data.frame(
    predictor = x_resid,
    response = y_resid,
    variable = var
  )
  return(df)
}

# 3. Build combined dataset for all retained predictors
partial_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(retained_vars, get_partial_df, 
                                    model = full_mod, data = std_vars))

# 4. Plot partial regression slopes
step.mod_partial_slopes <-
  ggplot(partial_df, aes(x = predictor, y = response)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "blue") + #95% CI
  facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(
    x = "Predictor (residuals)",
    y = "Response (residuals)",
    title = "Standardized Partial Regression Plots of Predictors"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

step.mod_partial_slopes

# Save
ggsave(
  filename = file.path(out_dir, "Partial_slopes_MLR.png"),
  plot     = step.mod_partial_slopes,
  width    = 8,
  height   = 6,
  dpi      = 300
)
```

## 4. Outlier detection

```{r}
# 1. Get model diagnostics
model_diag <- influence.measures(full_mod)

# 2. Extract indices of influential points flagged by diagnostics
infl_points <- which(apply(model_diag$is.inf, 1, any))

# 3. Create a dataframe with their info
flagged_obs <- data.frame(
  Sample_ID = dat$Sample_ID[infl_points],
  Fitted = fitted(full_mod)[infl_points],
  Residual = residuals(full_mod)[infl_points],
  Std_Residual = rstandard(full_mod)[infl_points],
  Leverage = hatvalues(full_mod)[infl_points],
  Cooks_D = cooks.distance(full_mod)[infl_points])

# View flagged observations
flagged_obs

# Save
library(openxlsx)

write.xlsx(
  flagged_obs,
  file = file.path(out_dir, "MLR_flagged_obs.xlsx"),
  overwrite = TRUE
)
```

Determine whether these flagged observations are clustered around a certain characteristic

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# 1. Add descriptive variables from dat to flagged observations (already done)

# 5. Combine plots
```

## 1. Summary Statistics

Mean and standard error by typology

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# Standard error function
se <- function(x) {
  sd(x, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(x)))
}

# Mode function (returns the most frequent value)
get_mode <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (length(x) == 0) return(NA)
  ux <- unique(x)
  ux[which.max(tabulate(match(x, ux)))]
}

summary_table <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(Typology, where(is.numeric)) %>%  # keep Typology + numeric vars
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -Typology,
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  group_by(Variable, Typology) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean     = mean(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median   = median(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
    Mode     = get_mode(Value),
    Variance = var(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
    SE       = se(Value),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

summary_table
```

## 2. Check of ANOVA Assumptions

### a. Normality

By Shapiro-Wilk

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(writexl)

# Set alpha for normality
alpha <- 0.05

# Identify numeric variables (same as before)
numeric_vars <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  names()

# Initialize results dataframe
shapiro_results <- data.frame(
  Variable = character(),
  W_statistic = numeric(),
  p_value = numeric(),
  Normal = logical(),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Loop over variables
for (var in numeric_vars) {
  
  # Remove NA values (required for Shapiro test)
  x <- dat[[var]]
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  
  # Shapiro test only works for 3 <= n <= 5000
  if (length(x) >= 3 && length(x) <= 5000) {
    
    test <- shapiro.test(x)
    
    W_val <- test$statistic
    p_val <- test$p.value
    
    normal <- p_val > alpha
    
  } else {
    # If sample size invalid, return NA
    W_val <- NA
    p_val <- NA
    normal <- NA
  }
  
  # Append results
  shapiro_results <- rbind(
    shapiro_results,
    data.frame(
      Variable = var,
      W_statistic = W_val,
      p_value = p_val,
      Normal = normal
    )
  )
}

# View results
shapiro_results

# Save
library(openxlsx)

# Load the existing workbook
wb <- loadWorkbook("Statistical_analyses_by_typology.xlsx")

# Create sheet if it does NOT exist
if(!"Normality by Shapiro Wilk" %in% names(wb)) {
  addWorksheet(wb, "Normality by Shapiro Wilk")
}

# Write your new table
writeData(wb, "Normality by Shapiro Wilk", shapiro_results)

# Save the workbook (overwrite)
saveWorkbook(wb, "Statistical_analyses_by_typology.xlsx", overwrite = TRUE)
```

### b. Homogeneity of Variance

Using the Levene Test

```{r}
library(car)  # for leveneTest()
library(dplyr)

# Set alpha for homogeneity check
alpha <- 0.05

# Identify all numeric variables EXCEPT Typology
numeric_vars <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  names()

# Initialize results dataframe
levene_results <- data.frame(
  Variable = character(),
  F_value = numeric(),
  p_value = numeric(),
  Homogeneous = logical(),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Loop over all numeric variables
for (var in numeric_vars) {
  
  # Run Levene's test
  test <- car::leveneTest(as.formula(paste(var, "~ Typology")), data = dat)
  
  # Extract F and p-values
  F_val <- test[1, "F value"]
  p_val <- test[1, "Pr(>F)"]
  
  # Determine homogeneity
  homogeneous <- p_val > alpha
  
  # Add results to dataframe
  levene_results <- rbind(
    levene_results, 
    data.frame(
      Variable = var,
      F_value = F_val,
      p_value = p_val,
      Homogeneous = homogeneous
    )
  )
}

# View results
levene_results

# Save
library(openxlsx)

# Load the existing workbook
wb <- loadWorkbook("Statistical_analyses_by_typology.xlsx")

# Create sheet if it does NOT exist
if(!"Homog Var by Typology" %in% names(wb)) {
  addWorksheet(wb, "Homog Var by Typology")
}

# Write your new table
writeData(wb, "Homog Var by Typology", levene_results)

# Save the workbook (overwrite)
saveWorkbook(wb, "Statistical_analyses_by_typology.xlsx", overwrite = TRUE)
```

## 3. Kruskal Wallis Test

Since most variables fail the assumptions for an ANOVA, we will use a non-parametric rank-based test to determine whether variables significantly differ by stream typology; the Kruskal Wallis (KW) test. We will also use the Holm-Bonferroni correction factor for multiple comparisons when conducting pairwise comparisons of variables by typology.

KW test relies on the following assumptions

1.  ***For ordinal, interval, or ratio data:*** While most of our variables fail this assumption, we can make an exception while being aware of this.

2.  ***The samples are independent of each other and within each group:*** Our variables meet this assumption.

3.  ***The distributions of the groups should have the same shape.***

### i. Distribution of variables by typology

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Choose variables whose distributions you want to compare by Typology
blm_predictors <- c(
  "log_Cu_uM",
  "log_Temp_C", 
  "pH", 
  "log_DOC_uM",
  "log_DIC_uM", 
  "log_Cl_uM", 
  "log_Ca_uM",
  "log_Mg_uM", 
  "log_SO4_uM", 
  "log_Na_uM",
  "log_K_uM"
)

# Change to long format
dat_long <- dat %>%
  # Keep Typology and the variables you want to check
  dplyr::select(Typology, all_of(blm_predictors)) %>%
  
  # Turn columns into rows: Variable, Value
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = -Typology,
    names_to  = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"
  )

# Density plots by Typology
ggplot(dat_long, aes(x = Value, fill = Typology)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.4) +   # alpha for transparent fill
  facet_wrap(~ Variable, scales = "free") +  # one panel per Variable
  labs(
    title = "Distributions by Typology",
    x = "Value",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1)
  )
```

### ii. Check for missing values

The KW test also can't handle variables with missing values and no variance, we'll check to see if any variables have these two conditions

```{r}

na_counts <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~sum(is.na(.)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(),
               names_to = "Variable",
               values_to = "NA_count") %>%
  filter(NA_count > 0)

# View results, should be 0
na_counts

dat$log_Upstream_from_main_stem_km <- NULL
```

### iii. Check for zero variance

No variables have missing values, now we'll check for lack of variance

```{r}
no_variance <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~dplyr::n_distinct(., na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(),
               names_to = "Variable",
               values_to = "Distinct_values") %>%
  filter(Distinct_values <= 1)

# View results, should be 0
no_variance
```

### iv. Run KW tests

Now we can perform the KW test

```{r}
library(tibble)
library(agricolae)
library(dplyr)

alpha <- 0.05

# 1. Get all numeric variables in dat
numeric_vars <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  names()

# 2. Create an empty list to store rows
combined_list <- list()

# 3. Loop through each numeric variable 
i <- 1
for (v in numeric_vars) {
  
  # Kruskal-Wallis test
  formula <- as.formula(paste(v, "~ Typology"))
  kw_test <- kruskal.test(formula, data = dat)
  
  chi_sq     <- kw_test$statistic
  df_val     <- kw_test$parameter
  p_val      <- kw_test$p.value
  significant <- p_val < alpha   # significant when p < 0.05
  
  # agricolae::kruskal to assign groups (letters)
  k_out <- agricolae::kruskal(
    y    = dat[[v]],
    trt  = dat$Typology,
    alpha = alpha,
    group = TRUE
  )
  
  # Create a data frame from the groups table
  groups_df <- k_out$groups %>%
    rownames_to_column("Typology")
  
  # Combine test results with group letters
  combined_list[[i]] <- groups_df %>%
    mutate(
      Variable   = v,
      Chi_sq     = as.numeric(chi_sq),
      df         = as.numeric(df_val),
      p_value    = as.numeric(p_val),
      Significant = significant
    )
  
  i <- i + 1
}

# 5. Bind everything together
combined_kruskal <- bind_rows(combined_list)

# View
combined_kruskal
```

Export to excel

```{r}
library(openxlsx)

# Load the existing workbook
wb <- loadWorkbook("Statistical_analyses_by_typology.xlsx")

  addWorksheet(wb, "K-W test by Typology")
}

# Write your new table
writeData(wb, "K-W test by Typology", combined_kruskal)

# Save the workbook (overwrite)
saveWorkbook(wb, "Statistical_analyses_by_typology.xlsx", overwrite = TRUE)
```

```{r}
# 3. Colors for each Typology
```

### a. Trace element fractions

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 1. Colors by response variable
#-------------------------------------------------
response_colors <- c(
  "Total Cu (nM)"       = "chocolate4",
  "Free Cu (nM)"        = "peru",
  "Free Cu2+/Total (%)" = "chocolate1",
  "Bioavailable Cu"     = "tan4"
)

# Facet order
response_order <- c(
  "Total Cu (nM)",
  "Free Cu (nM)",
  "Free Cu2+/Total (%)",
  "Bioavailable Cu"
)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 2. Define letter nudges
#-------------------------------------------------
letter_nudge <- c(
  "Total Cu (nM)"       = 1,
  "Free Cu (nM)"        = 1,
  "Free Cu2+/Total (%)" = 0.05,
  "Bioavailable Cu"     = 2
)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 3. Map variable names -> response labels
#-------------------------------------------------
response_lookup <- c(
  "log_Cu_nM"         = "Total Cu (nM)",
  "log_Free_Cu_nM"    = "Free Cu (nM)",
  "rel_prop_Cu"       = "Free Cu2+/Total (%)",
  "log_TBL_Cu_nmol_g" = "Bioavailable Cu"
)

vars_trace <- names(response_lookup)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 4. Long data
#-------------------------------------------------
dat_long_trace <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(Typology, all_of(vars_trace)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = -Typology,
    names_to  = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Value)) %>%
  mutate(
    Response = response_lookup[Variable],
    Response = factor(Response, levels = response_order)
  )

#-------------------------------------------------
# 5a. Max y per Variable x Typology
#-------------------------------------------------
y_pos_df <- dat_long_trace %>%
  group_by(Variable, Typology) %>%
  summarise(y_max = max(Value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

#-------------------------------------------------
# 5b. Attach letters above groups
#-------------------------------------------------
letters_long_trace <- letters_df %>%
  filter(Variable %in% vars_trace) %>%
  mutate(
    Response = response_lookup[Variable],
    Response = factor(Response, levels = response_order)
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    y_pos_df,
    by = c("Variable", "Typology")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    y_pos = y_max + letter_nudge[as.character(Response)]
  )

#-------------------------------------------------
# 5c. Facet strip labels with a., b., c., d.
#-------------------------------------------------
facet_labs <- c(
  "Total Cu (nM)"       = "a.~Total~Cu~(nM)",
  "Free Cu (nM)"        = "b.~Free~Cu^{2*'+'}~(nM)",
  "Free Cu2+/Total (%)" = "c.~Free~Cu^{2*'+'}/Total~Cu~('%')",
  "Bioavailable Cu"     = "d.~Bioavailable~Cu~(nmol~g^{-1}~wet)"
)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 6. Plot
#-------------------------------------------------
bioavail_panel2 <- ggplot(
  dat_long_trace,
  aes(
    x     = Typology,
    y     = Value,
    color = Response,
    fill  = Response
  )
) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.6, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 1, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_text(
    data = letters_long_trace,
    aes(x = Typology, y = y_pos, label = Letters),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = response_colors, breaks = response_order) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = response_colors, breaks = response_order) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ Response,
    scales = "free_y",
    ncol = 2,
    labeller = labeller(
      Response = as_labeller(facet_labs, label_parsed)
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10, angle = 30, hjust = 1, color = "black"),
    strip.text  = element_text(size = 12),
    plot.title  = element_text(size = 14)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Trace Elements by Stream Typology",
    x     = "Stream Typology",
    y     = expression(paste("Value [", log[10], "]"))
  )

bioavail_panel2

# Save
out_dir <- "Plots by typology"
if (!dir.exists(out_dir)) dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE)

ggsave(
  filename = file.path(out_dir, "Trace_elements_panel_Cu.png"),
  plot     = bioavail_panel2,
  width    = 8,
  height   = 8,
  dpi      = 300
)
```

```{r}
  ) +

  scale_color_manual(values = typology_colors, drop = FALSE) +

  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +

    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 9, angle = 30, hjust = 1, color = "black"),

    plot.title   = element_text(size = 14)
  )

spec_panel

# Save
ggsave(
  filename = file.path(out_dir, "Inorganic_Cu_complexes.png"),

)
```

### d. All species as relative proportion

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 1. Define variables of interest
#-------------------------------------------------
vars <- c(
  "Free_Cu_nM",
  "CuOH_nM",
  "Cu_OH_2_nM",
  "CuCO3_nM",
  "Cu_CO3_2_nM",
  "CuHCO3_nM",
  "CuSO4_nM",
  "CuCl_nM",
  "TOrg_Cu_nM"
)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 2. Set typology order
#-------------------------------------------------
dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    Typology = factor(
      Typology,
      levels = c("Pooled", "Non-Perennial", 
                 "Perennial", "Developed Perennial", "Main Stem")
    )
  )

#-------------------------------------------------
# 3. Pivot + summarize mean concentrations
#-------------------------------------------------
plot_dat <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(Typology, all_of(vars)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(vars),
    names_to = "Species",
    values_to = "conc_nM"
  ) %>%
  group_by(Typology, Species) %>%
  summarize(
    mean_conc = mean(conc_nM, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Species = Species %>%
      gsub("_nM", "", .) %>%
      gsub("_", " ", .),
    
    Species = dplyr::recode(
      Species,
      "Free Cu"  = "Cu²⁺",
      "CuOH"     = "CuOH",
      "Cu OH 2"  = "Cu(OH)₂",
      "CuCO3"    = "CuCO₃",
      "Cu CO3 2" = "Cu(CO₃)₂",
      "CuHCO3"   = "CuHCO₃",
      "CuSO4"    = "CuSO₄",
      "CuCl"     = "CuCl",
      "TOrg Cu"  = "Organic-Cu"
    )
  )

#-------------------------------------------------
# 4. Order species by total contribution
#-------------------------------------------------
plot_dat$Species <- factor(
  plot_dat$Species,
  levels = plot_dat %>%
    group_by(Species) %>%
    summarize(total = sum(mean_conc, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(desc(total)) %>%
    pull(Species)
)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 5. Fixed colors for Cu species
#-------------------------------------------------
custom_colors <- c(
  "Cu²⁺"       = "orange3",
  "CuOH"       = "orange1",
  "Cu(OH)₂"    = "yellow",
  "CuCO₃"      = "royalblue",
  "Cu(CO₃)₂"   = "skyblue",
  "CuHCO₃"     = "darkblue",
  "CuSO₄"      = "gold",
  "CuCl"       = "lightgreen",
  "Organic-Cu" = "brown"
)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 6. Plot stacked barplot
#-------------------------------------------------
cu_species <- ggplot(plot_dat, aes(x = Typology, y = mean_conc, fill = Species)) +
  geom_col(color = "black") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = custom_colors) +
  labs(
    x = "Typology",
    y = "Total Cu (nM)",
    fill = "Cu Species",
    title = "Copper Speciation by Typology"
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1)
  )

cu_species

#-------------------------------------------------
# 7. Save
#-------------------------------------------------
ggsave(
  filename = file.path(out_dir, "All_Cu_Complexes.png"),
  plot     = cu_species,
  width    = 7,
  height   = 5,
  dpi      = 300
)
```

Table

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

rel_table <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    total_cu_nM = rowSums(across(all_of(vars)), na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  filter(total_cu_nM > 0) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(vars),
    names_to = "Species",
    values_to = "conc_nM"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    rel_conc = conc_nM / total_cu_nM
  ) %>%
  group_by(Typology, Species) %>%
  summarize(
    Mean   = mean(rel_conc, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    SD     = sd(rel_conc, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    Median = median(rel_conc, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  )


# Wide format (Mean %)

rel_table_wide <- rel_table %>%
  dplyr::select(Typology, Species, Mean) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Species,
    values_from = Mean
  )

rel_table_wide

# Save
library(openxlsx)

write.xlsx(
  rel_table_wide,
  file = file.path(out_dir, "Cu_species_relative_proportions.xlsx"),
  overwrite = TRUE
)
```

### e. Publication plot

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
library(ggnewscale)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 1. Typology order
#-------------------------------------------------
dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    Typology = factor(
      Typology,
      levels = c(
        "Pooled",
        "Non-Perennial",
        "Perennial",
        "Developed Perennial",
        "Main Stem"
      )
    )
  )

#-------------------------------------------------
# 2. Stacked barplot data: Cu species
#-------------------------------------------------
species_vars <- c(
  "Free_Cu_nM",
  "CuOH_nM",
  "Cu_OH_2_nM",
  "CuCO3_nM",
  "Cu_CO3_2_nM",
  "CuHCO3_nM",
  "CuSO4_nM",
  "CuCl_nM",
  "TOrg_Cu_nM"
)

species_dat <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(Typology, all_of(species_vars)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(species_vars),
    names_to = "Species",
    values_to = "conc_nM"
  ) %>%
  group_by(Typology, Species) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_conc = mean(conc_nM, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Panel = "a.~Cu~speciation~(nM)",
    Species = dplyr::recode(
      Species,
      "Free_Cu_nM"    = "Cu²⁺",
      "CuOH_nM"       = "CuOH",
      "Cu_OH_2_nM"    = "Cu(OH)₂",
      "CuCO3_nM"      = "CuCO₃",
      "Cu_CO3_2_nM"   = "Cu(CO₃)₂",
      "CuHCO3_nM"     = "CuHCO₃",
      "CuSO4_nM"      = "CuSO₄",
      "CuCl_nM"       = "CuCl",
      "TOrg_Cu_nM"    = "Organic-Cu"
    )
  )

species_levels <- species_dat %>%
  group_by(Species) %>%
  summarise(total = sum(mean_conc, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(total)) %>%
  pull(Species)

species_dat <- species_dat %>%
  mutate(Species = factor(Species, levels = species_levels))

species_colors <- c(
  "Cu²⁺"       = "orange3",
  "CuOH"       = "orange1",
  "Cu(OH)₂"    = "yellow",
  "CuCO₃"      = "royalblue",
  "Cu(CO₃)₂"   = "skyblue",
  "CuHCO₃"     = "darkblue",
  "CuSO₄"      = "gold",
  "CuCl"       = "lightgreen",
  "Organic-Cu" = "brown"
)

species_colors <- species_colors[species_levels]

#-------------------------------------------------
# 3. Boxplot data: free/total Cu and bioavailable Cu
#-------------------------------------------------
box_lookup <- c(
  "rel_prop_Cu"       = "b.~Free~Cu^{2*'+'}/Total~Cu~('%')",
  "log_TBL_Cu_nmol_g" = "c.~Bioavailable~Cu~(nmol~g^{-1}~wet)~'['~log[10]~']'"
)

box_colors <- c(
  "b.~Free~Cu^{2*'+'}/Total~Cu~('%')" = "darkgray",
  "c.~Bioavailable~Cu~(nmol~g^{-1}~wet)~'['~log[10]~']'" = "darkslategray"
)

box_dat <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(Typology, all_of(names(box_lookup))) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -Typology,
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Value)) %>%
  mutate(
    Panel = box_lookup[Variable],
    Panel = factor(
      Panel,
      levels = c(
        "a.~Cu~speciation~(nM)",
        "b.~Free~Cu^{2*'+'}/Total~Cu~('%')",
        "c.~Bioavailable~Cu~(nmol~g^{-1}~wet)~'['~log[10]~']'"
      )
    )
  )

species_dat <- species_dat %>%
  mutate(
    Panel = factor(
      Panel,
      levels = levels(box_dat$Panel)
    )
  )

#-------------------------------------------------
# 4. Letters for boxplot panels only
#-------------------------------------------------
letter_nudge <- c(
  "b.~Free~Cu^{2*'+'}/Total~Cu~('%')" = 0.005,
  "c.~Bioavailable~Cu~(nmol~g^{-1}~wet)~'['~log[10]~']'" = 0.7
)

letters_box <- letters_df %>%
  filter(Variable %in% names(box_lookup)) %>%
  mutate(
    Panel = box_lookup[Variable],
    Panel = factor(Panel, levels = levels(box_dat$Panel))
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    box_dat %>%
      group_by(Variable, Typology) %>%
      summarise(y_max = max(Value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop"),
    by = c("Variable", "Typology")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    y_pos = y_max + letter_nudge[as.character(Panel)]
  )

letters_species <- letters_df %>%
  filter(Variable == "Cu_nM") %>%
  mutate(
    Panel = factor(
      "a.~Cu~speciation~(nM)",
      levels = levels(box_dat$Panel)
    )
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    species_dat %>%
      group_by(Typology) %>%
      summarise(y_max = sum(mean_conc, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop"),
    by = "Typology"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    y_pos = y_max + 20
  )

# Cu error bars
cu_error <- dat %>%
  group_by(Typology) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_Cu = mean(Cu_nM, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_Cu   = sd(Cu_nM, na.rm = TRUE),
    n       = sum(!is.na(Cu_nM)),
    se_Cu   = sd_Cu / sqrt(n),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    species_dat %>%
      group_by(Typology) %>%
      summarise(bar_height = sum(mean_conc, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop"),
    by = "Typology"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Panel = factor("a.~Cu~speciation~(nM)", levels = levels(species_dat$Panel)),
    ymin = bar_height - se_Cu,
    ymax = bar_height + se_Cu
  )

#-------------------------------------------------
# 5. Combined faceted plot
#-------------------------------------------------
cu_combined_panel <- ggplot() +
  
  geom_col(
    data = species_dat,
    aes(x = Typology, y = mean_conc, fill = Species),
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = species_colors,
    name = "Cu species",
    guide = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
  ) +
  
  geom_errorbar(
    data = cu_error,
    aes(x = Typology, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    width = 0.5,
    linewidth = 0.5,
    color = "black"
  ) +
  
  ggnewscale::new_scale_fill() +
  
  geom_boxplot(
    data = box_dat,
    aes(x = Typology, y = Value, fill = Panel, color = Panel),
    width = 0.7,
    alpha = 0.4,
    linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_jitter(
    data = box_dat,
    aes(x = Typology, y = Value, color = Panel),
    width = 0.15,
    size = 0.7,
    alpha = 0.7
  ) +
  
  geom_text(
    data = letters_species,
    aes(x = Typology, y = y_pos, label = Letters),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  
  geom_text(
    data = letters_box,
    aes(x = Typology, y = y_pos, label = Letters),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  
  scale_fill_manual(values = box_colors, guide = "none") +
  scale_color_manual(values = box_colors, guide = "none") +
  
  facet_wrap(
    ~ Panel,
    scales = "free_y",
    ncol = 3,
    labeller = labeller(Panel = label_parsed)
  ) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Copper Speciation and Bioavailability by Stream Typology",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Value"
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
```

### f. BL-bound cations

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Variables you want in the panel
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
vars_spec <- c(
  "log_BL_Ca_nmol_g",
  "log_BL_H_nmol_g",
  "log_BL_Mg_nmol_g",
  "log_BL_Na_nmol_g"
)

title_lookup <- c(
  "log_BL_Ca_nmol_g" = "BL-Ca",
  "log_BL_H_nmol_g"  = "BL-H",
  "log_BL_Mg_nmol_g" = "BL-Mg",
  "log_BL_Na_nmol_g" = "BL-Na"
)

facet_labels <- as_labeller(title_lookup)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2) Long data (DO NOT re-factor / reorder Typology)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
dat_long_spec <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(Typology, all_of(vars_spec)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = -Typology,
    names_to  = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Value)) %>%
  mutate(
    Variable = factor(Variable, levels = vars_spec)
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3) Letters (Kruskal groups) + y positions
#     letters_df must have: Variable, Typology, Letters
#     (DO NOT re-factor Typology here either)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
y_pos_df_spec <- dat_long_spec %>%
  group_by(Variable, Typology) %>%
  summarise(y_max = max(Value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

letters_long_spec <- letters_df %>%
  filter(Variable %in% vars_spec) %>%
  left_join(y_pos_df_spec, by = c("Variable", "Typology")) %>%
  mutate(
    y_pos = y_max + 0.05 * (abs(y_max) + 1)
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4) Faceted panel (FILLED boxplot + jitter), colored by Typology
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
spec_panel3 <- ggplot(dat_long_spec, aes(x = Typology, y = Value)) +
  geom_boxplot(
    aes(color = Typology, fill = Typology),
    width = 0.6,
    alpha = 0.35,
    outlier.shape = NA
  ) +
  geom_jitter(
    aes(color = Typology),
    width = 0.15,
    size  = 1.3,
    alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = letters_long_spec,
    aes(x = Typology, y = y_pos, label = Letters),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 3
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = typology_colors, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = typology_colors, drop = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ Variable,
    scales   = "free_y",
    ncol     = 2,
    labeller = facet_labels
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Biotic Ligand-Bound Cations by Stream Typology",
    x     = "Stream Typology",
    y     = "Log10(Concentration) (nmol g-1)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 9, angle = 30, hjust = 1),
    strip.text   = element_text(size = 11),
    plot.title   = element_text(size = 14)
  )
```

## 2. Overlap of measured vs toxic concentrations

Calculate probability of overlapping measured copper with toxic levels of copper by stream typology

```{r}
#Quantify overlapping area of measured copper with toxic concentrations by typology

# Extract the two vectors
x1 <- dat$log_Cu_nM
x2 <- dat$log_Cu_Chronic_Tox_Daphnia_nM
x3 <- dat$log_Cu_Acute_Tox_Daphnia_nM
x4 <- dat$log_Cu_Chronic_Tox_Minnow_nM
x5 <- dat$log_Cu_Acute_Tox_Minnow_nM

# Compute density overlaps between measured Cu and toxicity thresholds
library(dplyr)

overlap_area <- function(x, y, n = 512) {
  d1 <- density(x, n = n)
  d2 <- density(y, n = n)
  
  # Common x grid
  x_common <- seq(max(min(d1$x), min(d2$x)), min(max(d1$x), max(d2$x)), length.out = n)
  
  y1 <- approx(d1$x, d1$y, x_common)$y
  y2 <- approx(d2$x, d2$y, x_common)$y
  
  # Area under the minimum of both density curves
  overlap <- sum(pmin(y1, y2)) * diff(x_common[1:2])
  return(overlap)
}

# --- Compute overlaps by Typology ---
overlap_results_by_typology <- dat %>%
  group_by(Typology) %>%
  summarise(
    
    Overlap_Chronic_Toxicity_Daphnia = 
      overlap_area(log_Cu_nM, log_Cu_Chronic_Tox_Daphnia_nM),
    
    Overlap_Acute_Toxicity_Daphnia   = 
      overlap_area(log_Cu_nM, log_Cu_Acute_Tox_Daphnia_nM),
    
    Overlap_Chronic_Toxicity_Minnow  = 
      overlap_area(log_Cu_nM, log_Cu_Chronic_Tox_Minnow_nM),
    
    Overlap_Acute_Toxicity_Minnow    = 
      overlap_area(log_Cu_nM, log_Cu_Acute_Tox_Minnow_nM)
  
    ) %>%
  ungroup()

# View
overlap_results_by_typology
```

## 3. MLE of Cu toxicity

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)

# Raw toxicity variables ----
vars <- c(
  "Cu_Chronic_Tox_Daphnia_nM",
  "Cu_Acute_Tox_Daphnia_nM",
  "Cu_Chronic_Tox_Minnow_nM",
  "Cu_Acute_Tox_Minnow_nM"
)

mle_summary <- map_dfr(vars, function(var) {
  
  dat %>%
    dplyr::select(Typology, all_of(var)) %>%
    rename(value = all_of(var)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(Typology), !is.na(value)) %>%
    group_by(Typology) %>%
    summarise(
      variable = var,
      n = n(),
      mle_mean = mean(value),                    # μ̂
      mle_variance = mean((value - mean(value))^2),  # σ̂² with denominator n
      mle_sd = sqrt(mle_variance),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(Typology, variable, n, mle_mean, mle_variance, mle_sd)
})

mle_summary

)

    ) %>%

})
```

## 4. Relative proportion at or above toxicity threshold

### a. Daphnia

#### i. Chronic toxicity

```{r}
library(dplyr)

dat <- dat %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    prop_chronic_tox_daph = case_when(
      log_Cu_M >= log_Cu_Chronic_Tox_Daphnia_M ~ "On-Above",
      log_Cu_M < log_Cu_Chronic_Tox_Daphnia_M ~ "Below"
    )
  )

# Count the proportion On-Above

  count(prop_chronic_tox_daph) %>%
  mutate(
    proportion = n / sum(n),
    percent = proportion * 100
  )

prop_chronic_tox_daph_summary
```

```{r}
# Identify sample IDs on or above toxicity threshold
samples_above_chronic_tox_threshold_daph <- dat %>%
  filter(prop_chronic_tox_daph == "On-Above") %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Site,
    Sample_ID,
    Typology,
      log_Cu_nM,
      log_DOC_nM,
      pH,
      log_BL_Cu_nmol_g 
  )

# Calculate z-scores using summary_table

samples_above_chronic_tox_threshold_daph_zscores <- 
  samples_above_chronic_tox_threshold_daph %>%
  
  # Make data long so each variable can match summary_table
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      log_Cu_nM,
      log_DOC_nM,
      pH,
      log_BL_Cu_nmol_g
    ),
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  
  # Join mean and variance by Typology + Variable
  left_join(
    summary_table %>%
      dplyr::select(Variable, Typology, Mean, Variance),
    by = c("Variable", "Typology")
  ) %>%
  
  # Calculate SD and z-score
  mutate(
    SD = sqrt(Variance),
    z_score = (Value - Mean) / SD
  ) %>%
  
  # Make wider again
  dplyr::select(
    Site,
    Sample_ID,
    Typology,
    Variable,
    Value,
    z_score
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Variable,
    values_from = c(Value,  z_score)
  )
```

```{r}
# Count the proportion On-Above
prop_chronic_tox_min_summary <- dat %>%
  count(prop_chronic_tox_min) %>%
  mutate(
    proportion = n / sum(n),
    percent = proportion * 100
  )

prop_chronic_tox_min_summary
```

Plot

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

chronic_plot_min <- ggplot(dat, aes(x = log_Cu_Chronic_Tox_Minnow_M , y = log_Cu_M)) +

  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +

chronic_plot_min
```

#### ii. Acute toxicity

```{r}
library(dplyr)

dat <- dat %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    prop_acute_tox_min = case_when(
      log_Cu_M >= log_Cu_Acute_Tox_Minnow_M ~ "On-Above",
      log_Cu_M < log_Cu_Acute_Tox_Minnow_M ~ "Below"
    )
  )

# Count the proportion On-Above
prop_acute_tox_min_summary <- dat %>%
  count(prop_acute_tox_min) %>%
  mutate(
    proportion = n / sum(n),
    percent = proportion * 100
  )
```

All plots

```{r}
library(patchwork)

# Create the top row

  plot_annotation(title = 'Daphnia')

# Create the bottom row
row2 <- (chronic_plot_min + acute_plot_min) + 
  plot_annotation(title = 'Fathead Minnow')

# Combine them
all_plots <- wrap_elements(row1) / wrap_elements(row2)
all_plots

  filename = file.path(out_dir, "Cu_tox_thresholds.png"),

  units = "in",
  dpi = 300
)
```

# Plots by Site within Typology

## 1. Main Stem

Total Cu

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(forcats)

mainstem_tblcu_plot_dat <- dat %>%
  filter(Typology == "Main Stem") %>%
  filter(!is.na(Cu_nM),
         !is.na(Upstream_from_main_stem_km),
         Cu_nM > 0) %>%   # needed for log10
  mutate(
    Site = fct_reorder(Site, Upstream_from_main_stem_km, .fun = max, .desc = TRUE),
    log10_Cu_nM = log10(Cu_nM)
  )

ms_plot <- ggplot(mainstem_tblcu_plot_dat, aes(x = Site, y = log10_Cu_nM)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Total dissolved Cu within the Main Stem",
    x = "Site (ordered by decreasing relative elevation)",
    y = expression(log[10]~"(TBL Cu, nM)")
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )

ms_plot
```

Only EFK sites

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(stringr)
library(forcats)

efk_plot_dat <- dat %>%
  filter(Typology == "Main Stem") %>%
  filter(str_starts(Site, "EFK")) %>%   # keep only EFK sites
  filter(!is.na(Cu_nM),
         Cu_nM > 0) %>%
  mutate(
    # Extract numeric part after "EFK"
    EFK_num = as.numeric(str_remove(Site, "EFK")),
    
    # Order factor by decreasing numeric value
    Site = fct_reorder(Site, EFK_num, .desc = TRUE),
    
    log10_Cu_nM = log10(Cu_nM)
  )

ggplot(efk_plot_dat, aes(x = Site, y = log10_Cu_nM)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Total Cu across EFK Main Stem Sites",
    x = "EFK Site (decreasing downstream order)",
    y = expression(log[10]~"(Cu (nM))")
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )

```
